source.authority: The built HTML/CSS is the truth; NOTES.md was the starting inventory.

ground.usage: Page background; every inset tile inside a white card; table row hover; tab bar tray; mini mock panel.

ground-deep.usage: Hero image slot; quiet pill and mute chip background.

card.usage: Every card, stat card, active tab, preview tile; bought-leg curve point fill; step-badge numeral. Appears as the literal #fff in the SVGs.

ink.usage: Primary text, wordmark, tickers, money figures, sold-leg point ring, text on lime.

ink-2.usage: Secondary text, captions, column headers, the Sell label, nav links, chart axis labels. 7.5:1 on white, 6.4:1 on ground.

ink-3.usage: Icon tint only (lock glyph, the isn't cross). Never text; fails AA on ground.

line.usage: 1px table rules; 1.5px outlines (secondary/ghost buttons, preview tiles, curve box); dashed payoff baselines; mini mock bars.

violet.usage: Links, pill text, highlighted-tile labels, step badge, Buy label, payoff curve stroke, gauge fill, focus ring, scrollbar thumb, secondary/ghost hover border. 5.5:1 on white, 4.9:1 on violet-soft.

violet-soft.usage: Highlight surface: used quote side, credit KPI/stat tile, default pill background, gauge track, violet chips.

lime.usage: Primary button, rank-1 disc, Free pill, graded/ok chip, sold-leg point fill, ::selection. Always carries ink text.

mini-bar-deep.usage: Darker bar/dot fill in mini mocks; the dotted SPY comparison curve. UNTOKENIZED in the source (literal #D9D2E3, reused 3x) — promote to a custom property before app use.

display.purpose: Hero headline only. Bricolage Grotesque 800, opsz 96, text-wrap: balance.

headline.purpose: Section headings and the closing card heading. Bricolage 700, opsz 72.

title.purpose: Card titles, It is / It isn't columns, tab labels (1rem), preview titles (1.25rem). Bricolage 700, opsz 24.

money.purpose: Dollar figures, strikes, percentages. Bricolage 800, tabular, always with a Figtree caption beneath. Sizes 1.35 / 1.6 / 1.7 / 2 / 2.2rem by context.

ticker.purpose: Symbol names. Bricolage 800 at 1.25 / 1.6 / 2rem; 700 at 1.05rem inside the table.

lede.purpose: The sentence after a heading. Figtree 400, 1.125rem, ink-2, max 66ch (38rem under a section heading).

table.purpose: Table cells. 0.95rem, tabular, nowrap; credit column 700.

label.purpose: Pill text and KPI keys. Figtree 600, 0.8rem, sentence case.

column-header.purpose: Table th. 0.78rem 600, ink-2, 0.03em tracking, sentence case.

chart-label.purpose: Strike labels under payoff points, in the leg's color. 11px in step cards, 12px in the dashboard.

numerics.rule: Every strike, credit, percentage, dollar figure and date carries .num
numerics.monoFont: none — tabular Figtree, not a monospace face

shadows.name: shadow
shadows.purpose: Rest. Every white card, stat card, and the active tab.

shadows.name: shadow-hover
shadows.purpose: Step cards on hover, with translateY(-2px) at 250ms ease.

shadows.name: shadow-lift
shadows.purpose: The front hero card only — the one surface above other cards.

shadows.name: shadow-primary
shadows.purpose: Lime primary button at rest (lime-tinted glow).

shadows.name: shadow-none
shadows.purpose: Highlighted (violet-soft) tiles, inset ground tiles, and outlined surfaces (1.5px line border) rest flat.

borders.name: outline
borders.purpose: Secondary/ghost buttons, preview tiles, curve box.

radii.rule: One radius, 24px, on every outer surface. Inner radii are derived: 18px = radius/2 + 6px for a container nested once inside a card (tab bar, preview tile, leg tile, curve box); 12px = radius/2 for a control inside that (tab, mini mock). 999px only for the miniature bars/dots/chips inside mini mocks.
radii.circles: 36px step badge and 26px rank marker use 24px and therefore render as full circles.

motion.name: ease-settle
motion.purpose: Every authored animation: hero settle, headline rise, curve draw, gauge fill.

motion.name: hero-settle
motion.value: settle .9s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) both; from { opacity:0; transform: translateY(28px) rotate(calc(var(--rot) + 2deg)) } to { opacity:1; transform: translateY(0) rotate(var(--rot)) }; delays .05s / .18s / .32s (back / mid / front); --rot -5deg / 3.5deg / 0deg
motion.purpose: On load, the three hero cards settle into their stack.

motion.name: hero-rise
motion.value: rise .7s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) both; from { opacity:0; transform: translateY(14px) }; children delayed 0 / .08s / .16s / .24s
motion.purpose: The headline block rises with the cards.

motion.name: curve-draw
motion.purpose: Dashboard payoff curve draws once when .dash gains .is-in (IntersectionObserver threshold .35, then disconnect).

motion.name: gauge-fill
motion.purpose: Probability gauge fills after the curve.

motion.name: hover-button
motion.value: transform, box-shadow, background-color, border-color .18s ease; translateY(-1px) on hover, 0 on active

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: All keyframes and the pre-animation offsets live inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference); under reduce the cards are at rest and the curve/gauge render settled with no script; the reveal script adds .is-in immediately when reduce is set or IntersectionObserver is absent.

breakpoints.name: tablet
breakpoints.changes: Hero, proof, scan-output grids → 1 column; steps stack; dashboard stacks with stats 4-up (gauge spans 2); previews 2-up; hero padding 32/64; hero visual +16px top margin.

breakpoints.name: nav
breakpoints.changes: Nav links hide; brand + ghost button remain.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.changes: Base 16px; section padding 64; card padding 24 (cluster 16); back hero cards hide, front card 88% wide, its stat row hidden, credit 1.7rem; leg tiles 1-up; stats 2-up with gauge full-width; tab bar wraps 2-up (10px 8px, .95rem, text may break); previews 1-up; honest card 1 column at 24 padding; closing card 64/16 padding.

layout.sectionPadding: 96px block (64px under 640px); hero 64 top / 96 bottom (32 / 64 under 980px)

grids.hero: 1.05fr 1fr, gap 64, align center; 4:3 slot with cluster absolutely positioned (back 62% left 2% top 6% rotate -5deg; mid 58% right 3% top 16% rotate 3.5deg; front 72% left 14% bottom 4%)
grids.dashboard: 1.15fr .85fr, gap 24; stat grid 1fr 1fr gap 16 with gauge grid-column 1 / -1

spacingScale.subScale: 6px and 10px appear as gaps inside compact rows (leg rows, tab bar padding, pill gaps)

comparisonCurve.note: Performance mini; the two curves end level.

openTokens.name: profit / loss pair
openTokens.note: No color for graded outcomes (win, loss, breakeven, borderline). Must be distinct from violet (structure) and lime (action), carry a text/sign cue, and never appear on chrome. Do not reuse lime.

openTokens.name: input / field
openTokens.note: No input exists in the artifact; the recipe in DESIGN.md and the ds-input component here are derived from the button and tile rules and need confirmation on first app build.

openTokens.name: error / warning / disabled
openTokens.note: No error, warning, or disabled state exists in the build.

openTokens.name: selected-row
openTokens.note: The ranked table has a hover fill (ground) but no selected state; the app needs one.

openTokens.name: mini-bar-deep
openTokens.note: #D9D2E3 reused 3x as a literal; promote to --mini-bar-deep (or fold into the line ramp).

openTokens.name: card literal
openTokens.note: #fff / #FFFFFF used directly in SVG point fills and the step-badge numeral instead of var(--card).

openTokens.name: dark theme
openTokens.note: This world is light-only; no dark palette is defined.

components.css: .ds-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px; font-family: 'Figtree', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif; color: #15121A; max-width: 360px; } .ds-field-label { font-size: .8rem; font-weight: 600; color: #5A5266; letter-spacing: .01em; } .ds-input { font: inherit; font-size: 1rem; color: #15121A; background: #FFFFFF; border: 1.5px solid #E3DEE9; border-radius: 24px; padding: 14px 20px; transition: border-color .18s ease; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #5A5266; } .ds-input:hover { border-color: #6547E6; } .ds-input:focus { border-color: #6547E6; } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #6547E6; outline-offset: 3px; }

narrative.overview:
Luo Capital's visual world treats an options trade as a physical object: three white cards you could pick up, turn over, and read the credit off the front. Everything sits on a pale, warm lilac-gray ground that is neither paper nor screen; white surfaces float above it on soft, downward-cast shadows; black ink does the talking; one flat violet draws the structure (links, labels, the "buy" leg, the payoff line); and one chartreuse is spent on exactly the thing we want the visitor to do. The density is deliberately low for a finance product: one focal point per section, generous section padding, a 66-character measure, and numbers set large in the display face so a $540 credit reads before a sentence does. It is calm on purpose, because the product's promise is that the number is real, and calm is how a real number looks.

This world was chosen as direction v1 ("Soft Fintech Cards") over four alternatives and then absorbed three components from the rejected v4 ("Friendly Data") direction, recolored into this palette: payoff-curve step cards, the tab-strip "What's inside" panel, and the setup dashboard with its drawn curve and probability gauge. Those are now native here, not borrowed. The old app frontend (dark slate, purple, JetBrains Mono) is superseded by this system and carries no authority.

Confirmed rejections, from the direction contract and the build: no dark terminal, no candlestick chaos, no dense tables above the fold, no gradients anywhere, no stock photography, no 3D blobs, no icon-grid feature rows, no purple-gradient SaaS, no fake proof.
keyCharacteristics: Warm lilac-gray ground with white cards on soft offset shadows; black ink; two flat accents (violet for structure, lime for the one action); no gradients.
One radius, 24px, on every outer surface; inner controls derive 12px and 18px from it.
Bricolage Grotesque for headings, tickers, and money; Figtree for everything else; every figure tabular.
The pay/collect convention runs through every component: bought leg = violet or white-with-violet-ring; sold legs = lime-with-ink-ring or muted ink.
One authored entrance (the hero cards settle) and one scroll reveal (the curve draws, the gauge fills); everything else is a 150 to 250 ms ease and all of it is off under reduced motion.

rules.name: The One Action Rule
rules.body: Lime appears only where the visitor can act or has been rewarded for acting: the primary button, the rank-1 marker, the Free pill, a graded/ok status chip, and the sold-leg point on a curve. It is never a background wash, never a border, never body text.

rules.name: The Pay/Collect Rule
rules.body: Anything the trader pays for is violet (the "Buy" label, the bought-leg curve point drawn white with a violet ring); anything the trader collects is ink or lime (the "Sell" label in ink-2, the sold-leg points drawn lime with an ink ring). The convention holds across the setup card, the leg tiles, the step cards, and the dashboard curve, so a reader learns it once.

rules.name: The Money Is Ink Rule
rules.body: Dollar figures, strikes, and percentages are set in ink, in the display face, with tabular figures. Money never borrows lime or violet, so the eye never confuses a value with an action or a status. (The build carries one exception, the "+ $540" result pill after the three steps; it is a rhetorical flourish on the marketing page, not a pattern for the app.)

rules.name: The Tinted Gray Rule
rules.body: No neutral gray anywhere. Every gray in the system is warmed toward the ground's lilac hue (ink-2, ink-3, line, ground-deep).

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every strike, credit, percentage, dollar figure, and date carries .num (font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-feature-settings: "tnum"). Tables carry it on the <table> element so every cell inherits it. This is what keeps numeric columns aligned without a monospace face.

rules.name: The Caption Under Money Rule
rules.body: A money figure is never alone: it always has its unit or condition beneath it in the body face (credit per contract, if NVDA is above $200, tied up while it's open), smaller and in ink-2.

rules.name: The Sentence-Case Rule
rules.body: No uppercase labels, no eyebrows, no kickers. Column headers and pill labels are sentence case with at most 0.03em of tracking.

rules.name: The Soft Offset Rule
rules.body: Every shadow is offset downward (y ≥ 8px), blurred at least 2.5× its offset, and tinted rgba(40, 30, 70, α) with α between .10 and .16. No spread, no inset, no black.

rules.name: The Highlight Tile Rule
rules.body: A highlighted tile (kpi.hi, dash-stat.hi, quote-side.used) swaps its background to violet-soft and its label to violet, and drops its shadow (box-shadow: none). The "used" quote side adds a 2px inset violet outline. Highlight is a color change, never an added shadow.

dos: Do put every outer surface on the 24px radius and derive inner radii as 18px (radius/2 + 6px) and 12px (radius/2); never pick a third value.
Do set every figure with .num (tabular-nums) and right-align numeric columns.
Do set money in Bricolage Grotesque 800 with tracking -0.02em and a Figtree caption in ink-2 beneath it.
Do draw the bought leg white-with-violet-ring and the sold legs lime-with-ink-ring on every payoff curve, and label "Buy" in violet and "Sell" in ink-2 on every leg list.
Do highlight the tile that is the point of a card by switching it to violet-soft with violet labels and no shadow.
Do keep shadows soft and offset downward in rgba(40, 30, 70, .10–.16); outline flat surfaces with 1.5px line instead.
Do house every animation inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference and render the settled state by default.
Do use ink-3 for icon tint only and ink-2 for any secondary text.
donts: Don't use lime for anything but the primary action, the rank-1 marker, Free/graded chips, and sold-leg curve points; never as a wash, border, or figure color.
Don't color a dollar figure violet or lime; money is ink.
Don't use gradients, zero-offset halo shadows, hard shadows, or pure neutral grays.
Don't set labels in uppercase, or add eyebrows or kickers above headings.
Don't introduce a monospace face for numbers; tabular Figtree is the rule.
Don't put a dark surface, a candlestick chart, or a dense table above the fold.
Don't reuse lime, violet, or an ad-hoc green/red for profit and loss; the pair is an open system decision and must carry a text or sign cue when it lands.
Don't reuse the untokenized #D9D2E3 or #fff literals from the landing page's SVGs and mini mocks without first promoting them to custom properties (mini-bar-deep, card).
